question: When did Republic Steel's funded Lorain mill (1807 E 28th St, Lorain County) stop producing?
answer: Resolved, and it overturns the premise. Steel melting at Lorain stopped in June 2015, and the entire Lorain facility was idled effective March 31, 2016. It never restarted. Grupo Simec, Republic Steel's parent, says so in ten consecutive Form 20-F annual reports to the SEC. The FY2016 20-F: 'In June of 2015 Republic Steel temporarily idled the newly constructed electric arc furnace at the Lorain, Ohio, facility' and 'Subsequent to year end, the entire Lorain facility was temporarily idled effective March 31, 2016 and at the date of issuance, March 30, 2017, management has no near-term plans to restart the facility.' Simec took a USD $130.7 million impairment on the Lorain melt shop in FY2015. Every 20-F from FY2018 through FY2024 then repeats, with only the year changing: 'This facility did not produce any steel billets or finished steel bars in [year] as it has been idled since 2016.' The per-facility production tables show Lorain at 0 tons against 816,000 to 1,049,000 tons of installed capacity, every year FY2018 through FY2024. The separate Lorain blast furnace 'has been idle since 2008.' Two EPA datasets agree independently. EPA's Greenhouse Gas Reporting Program, facility 1002714 'Republic Steel - Lorain Plant', 1807 E. 28th St.: Subpart Q, the iron-and-steel-production subpart, appears in 2014 (113,031 t CO2) and 2015 (86,313 t) and never again; 2016 is combustion-only at 15,299 t, an 82 percent drop; no report at all for 2017 through 2023, meaning the plant fell below the 25,000 tCO2e mandatory threshold. Republic's Canton plant (facility 1003799) filed every year from 2010 to 2023, so this is not a filing lapse. EPA's Toxics Release Inventory, facility 44055SSLRN1807E: on-site releases of 17,075 lbs in 2014, 2,854 in 2015, 8.5 in 2016, no forms for 2017 through 2020, 14.6 in 2021, 18.0 in 2022, none after; the facility carries fac_closed_ind = 1; the 2016 lead Form R reports a production ratio of 0.18 against 2015 and the 2021 and 2022 manganese and chromium forms report a production ratio of 0. One honest nuance: TRI reporting requires ten or more full-time-equivalent employees, so Republic had at least ten people at Lorain in 2021 and 2022, which fits JobsOhio's pleading that 55 of 125 jobs were created. The production ratios of zero say those people were not making steel. There is a real inconsistency inside Simec's own filings that the post should name rather than resolve silently: the production-table footnotes in the FY2023 and FY2024 20-Fs group Lorain with Canton, Lackawanna, Massillon and Solon as having 'ceased operations in August 2023', and the FY2025 20-F flips the year outright to 'This facility has been idled since 2023 and did not produce any steel billet or finished products in 2025, 2024 or 2023.' Nine earlier filings say 2016 and the zero-tonnage tables say 2016. The best reading is that August 2023 is when the residual site crew and the abandoned 9/10 inch mill recommissioning ended, swept up in the company-wide shutdown, not when steelmaking stopped. The FY2023 20-F also quotes the EPA Administrative Orders on Consent: 'the Lorain Facility will remain idle with no current plans to resume activities; and the Canton Facility is permanently shut down with no intention to reopen.' A Consent Decree was signed December 6, 2023. On the missing WARN notice: the Lorain mass layoff was in January 2016, years before the 2020-2026 window the project pulled, which is why no notice exists. No Lorain-area notice surfaced under SimRep, Republic Engineered Products, Nucor Steel Lorain or a staffing agency, and I confirmed directly against data/warn/notices.csv that the only Lorain steel notice in 2020-2026 is 'US Steel Seamless Tubular Operations (Lorain Tubular)', 250 affected, received 3/23/20, a different company at a different plant, and that the only Republic Steel notice in the whole register is Canton/Stark, 209 affected, received 8/22/23, separations 08/10/2023 to 08/23/2023.

question: AK Steel's funded site: Warren County, as JobsOhio's report says, or Butler County, where the payment went?
answer: Resolved, and there is no conflict once the site is named. The funded project is AK Steel's new Research and Innovation Center at 6180 Research Way, Middletown, Ohio 45005, and that parcel is in WARREN County. JobsOhio's August 2015 report is right about the county. 9227 Centre Pointe Drive, West Chester, the Butler County address on Schedule I, is just AK Steel's corporate headquarters, the remit-to address on the check. The reconciliation is not the one we guessed: it is not a Warren County parcel of Middletown Works. It is a separate 16-acre greenfield site in the Warren County part of the City of Middletown, east of I-75, in the Franklin City School District. AK Steel's own SEC-filed press release of 2015-02-23 says the company 'will build a new, world-class Research and Innovation Center in Middletown, Ohio,' a '120,000 square foot facility' on 'a 15-acre site located in the Cincinnati - Dayton growth corridor along Interstate 75,' at an estimated project cost of $36 million, and thanks 'the State of Ohio, City of Middletown, Warren County Port Authority, JobsOhio, and REDI (Regional Economic Development Initiative) Cincinnati.' The same release says the facility 'will be home to the company's approximately 75 researchers, scientists and engineers.' That 75 is JobsOhio's '75 retained,' exactly. The Warren County Port Authority's board minutes of 2015-03-16 record its director sharing 'the announcement of AK Steel's new R&D facility in Warren County... roughly $36 million investment and will bring about 75 new jobs.' Its minutes of 2015-05-18 set out the deal: the Port would hold a ground lease from the City of Middletown and a project lease with Fortress Capital, AK Steel's construction agent, and would put $30,000 toward electric infrastructure out of a $127,000 fee. The street address is pinned by Schedule 8.6.1, Business Locations, of AK Steel's Second Amended and Restated Loan and Security Agreement of 2017-09-13, which lists 'Research and Innovation Center, 6180 Research Way, Middletown, OH 45005' as a location separate from 'Middletown Works, 1801 Crawford Street, Middletown, OH 45043.' ZIP 45005 is Franklin, Warren County; 45042 through 45044 are the Butler County Middletown ZIPs. The Warren County Auditor's own parcel layer carries four Research Way parcels, including account 2434338 at 6180 Research Way, owner CITY OF MIDDLETOWN, 16.0 acres, use code 495 TIF, and account 2434406, same address, 32.0 acres, use code 710 Community Reinvestment, both in Middletown and the Franklin City School District. City ownership is exactly what the ground-lease structure requires, and a query of the same layer for owners containing 'AK STEEL' returns nothing, consistent with AK Steel leasing rather than owning. The FY2015 10-K says the company is 'currently constructing a new research and innovation center in Middletown to replace the existing building'; the FY2016 10-K says it moved in during the fourth quarter of 2016 and that the $36.0 million project was 'primarily financed through a $25.2 long-term capital lease' with an initial term expiring in 2034.

First, JobsOhio's $4,700,000 investment figure does not match the $36 million project and no public record explains the gap; it is probably a partial or eligible-cost figure, since AK Steel leased the building and the developer-financed shell was $25.2 million, but that is inference, not a document, and it deserves a line rather than a silent reconciliation. Second, the Ohio Tax Credit Authority is a dead end here and that is itself a finding: every archived TCA minute for 2015 and 2016 was downloaded and read, including OCR of the image-only scans, and AK Steel appears in none of them, so this project got no state Job Creation Tax Credit. Not reached: the Warren County Auditor's public web search (Cloudflare 403, so the county's own ArcGIS parcel service was used instead), REDI Cincinnati's 2015 annual report (Internet Archive intermittently offline), and the City of Middletown's site search (returns the same page for every query). The one document that would belt-and-brace this is the City of Middletown ordinance of spring 2015 authorizing the ground lease of the Research Way site to the Warren County Port Authority, with the matching Community Reinvestment Area agreement, both held by the Middletown Clerk of Council. The executed JobsOhio grant agreement, the only thing that would explain the $4.7 million figure, is obtainable only from JobsOhio, which is not subject to Ohio public records law.

question: What is Goodlevel Enterprises LLC and did anything happen to it?
answer: Resolved, and it clears the row. Goodlevel Enterprises LLC, EIN 81-4719550, 55 Newton St, Norwalk, Ohio, trades as THE MAPLE CITY RUBBER COMPANY. Maple City is Norwalk's nickname. The Department of Labor's EFAST2 Form 5500 public datasets record the plan sponsor verbatim as 'GOODLEVEL ENTERPRISES LLC DBA' with the plan named 'THE MAPLE CITY RUBBER COMPANY 401(K) PROFIT SHARING PLAN,' same EIN, same street address. That also explains the stray 'DBA' fragment on the 990 Schedule I row. The business code is 326100, plastics product manufacturing, on the 2023 through 2025 filings and 326200, rubber product manufacturing, on the 2020 filing; the plan's effective date is 1990-01-01, so the operating business long predates the 2016 LLC. The Ohio company is alive and growing. Form 5500-SF participant counts run 39 down to 26 for plan year 2020, 63 up to 76 for 2023, 77 to 78 for 2024, and 79 to 84 for 2025, with active participants going from 73 to 77 over 2025. The 2025 filing was received 2026-07-19, is signed, is not a final filing and shows plan assets rising from $1,112,885 to $1,342,788 with $40,498 of employer contributions. That active count of 73 to 77 independently corroborates the 74 retained in JobsOhio's February 2026 monthly report, from a different agency. The Canadian insolvency is real, is related, and is a different company. Goodlevel Enterprises Canada ULC is a Hamilton, Ontario manufacturer and distributor of latex balloons, created to acquire the assets of Pioneer Balloon Canada Limited out of Pioneer's own 2024 insolvency. It filed a proposal under the Bankruptcy and Insolvency Act on 2025-08-13 listing nearly $4 million of liabilities, about $3.3 million of it owed to Goodlevel Enterprises LLC, its US affiliate, with KPMG as proposal trustee and about 32 employees, all on temporary layoff at the filing date. The BC corporate registry confirms the entity: GOODLEVEL ENTERPRISES CANADA ULC, incorporation number BC1488108, incorporated 2024-06-20, status ACTIVE, renamed to its current name effective 2025-05-05. Note the direction of the money: the Ohio company is the Canadian entity's largest creditor, not a beneficiary of it, and the 32 layoffs are in Ontario.

question: Is Multi-Color's funded Batavia plant in Clermont County still operating?
answer: Resolved on documents rather than on the absence of a WARN notice. Four independent records say the site is live, two of them dated within the last two weeks. First, it is a real plant. Multi-Color's last 10-K as a public company, Item 2 Properties, 'As of March 31, 2019, the Company owned and leased the following 72 manufacturing facilities,' lists 'Batavia, Ohio (2)' at 392,527 square feet, owned and leased, as separate line items from Norwood (313,322, owned) and Mason (72,000, leased). Second, EPA says the air source is operating. The facility is in EPA's Facility Registry Service as registry ID 110033622293, 'MCC MANUFACTURING, INC.' / 'MULTI COLOR CORPORATION', 4053 Clough Woods Dr, Batavia, Clermont County. Its ECHO Detailed Facility Report shows ICIS-Air source OH0000001413020513 with FacilityStatus 'Operating', an 80 percent synthetic minor universe, a federally enforceable state operating permit, NAICS 323111 and 323112 commercial flexographic printing, an active RCRA handler record OHR000147462, and Clean Air Act compliance status reported for twelve consecutive quarters from Q1 2024 through Q4 2026, all 'No Violation Identified', current as of 2026-11-07 against an ICIS-Air extract date of 2026-11-06. The last full compliance evaluation was an on-site Ohio EPA inspection on 2022-08-02. question: What happened to Nostrum Laboratories' plant at 705 E Mulberry St, Bryan, Ohio, and when?
answer: Partly resolved. There is a tight bracket for when production stopped and a hard date for when the site left Nostrum's hands, but no document says 'ceased operations' on a given day and no Bryan job-loss figure is on the public record I could reach. Everything below is from the Chapter 11 docket, In re Nostrum Laboratories, Inc., No. 24-19611-JKS (Bankr. D.N.J.), read through the RECAP mirror on the Internet Archive. The JobsOhio-era expansion is documented: Waterford Bank, N.A.'s limited objection of 2025-05-15 states that 'By mortgage dated March 19, 2020 ... Waterford financed Debtor's expansion of its facilities located in Bryan, Ohio,' two months after JobsOhio's January 2020 report of the $250,000 grant against a $3,250,000 investment, which is the same expansion. The same filing describes the site as 'a 23,644 square foot warehouse and a 35,376 square foot manufacturing facility and two smaller buildings totaling about 6,600 square feet.' The parcels are listed in Schedule 2.1(c) of the asset purchase agreement: 705 E. Mulberry St., Williams County parcels 063-170-36-013.000 through -018.000, plus 604 E. Edgerton St. / E. Trevitt St. / 721-725 E. Mulberry St. The timeline: last documented production is 2025-03-03, from the 'In Process Inventory' schedule attached to the Prasco asset purchase agreement, which lists six batches of Nitrofurantoin Oral Suspension made at Bryan on 2025-02-25, 2025-02-26 and 2025-03-03, with nothing later anywhere in the record. The plant was still described as running on 2025-04-08, when the United States' limited objection, filed by the DOJ Civil Division for FDA, says 'The Debtor operates two drug manufacturing facilities, one in Bryan, OH and one in Kansas City, MO,' in the present tense. On 2025-04-14 the court approved the sale: Waterford Bank took the Bryan real property on a credit bid of $1,345,085, and Big Shoulders Capital XII, LLC and Federal Equipment Company took 'the equipment at the Bryan, OH facility' for $250,000, which ends manufacturing there by definition. On 2025-04-15 payroll failed: Citizens Bank's emergency motion says the debtor 'was unable to retain employees because it was unable to assure employees that the payroll due the week of April 18, 2025 would be made' and 'has been operating on a skeleton crew.' By 2025-04-29 a Waterford SVP visited and photographed about eight rows of racking holding 'miscellaneous expired products'; the finished-goods table lists 11,176 bottles of oxycodone and acetaminophen oral solution expired 01/2024 and 23,165 bottles of promethazine with codeine expired 06/2024. The same filing records 'more than 70,000 pounds of Schedule II Controlled Substances at the Debtor's Ohio location that must be disposed of,' which the buyer 'wants nothing to do with,' against a removal quote of $275,000. The safest sentence for the post: the Bryan plant's last recorded production run was 3 March 2025; its equipment and real estate were sold at a bankruptcy auction approved on 14 April 2025; payroll collapsed the next day; and by 29 April 2025 the site held only expired product and abandoned narcotics.

question: Was anything ever built in Licking County for AmplifyBio?
answer: Resolved, and it reverses the premise. Yes. A 351,846 square foot building was built, occupied and operated in Licking County for AmplifyBio, and it is still standing. The address is 9885 Innovation Campus Way, New Albany, Ohio 43054, in Jersey Township, Licking County, inside the New Albany International Business Park. AmplifyBio called it the Advanced Manufacturing Enablement Center, or AMEC. It opened in February 2024 and closed on 2025-04-04. AmplifyBio leased it and never owned Licking County land, which is why no auditor search in the company's name finds anything. The federal WARN class action names both sites: Freeman v. AmplifyBio, LLC, Case 2:25-cv-00561-ALM-EPD (S.D. Ohio), class action complaint filed 2025-05-20, paragraphs 2 and 3: 'Defendant AmplifyBio, LLC, operated two facilities in the Columbus area: one at 1425 Plain City-Georgesville Road, West Jefferson, Ohio 43162 ... and another at 9885 Innovation Campus Way, New Albany, Ohio 43054 ... where Plaintiff and other similarly situated employees worked,' and 'On or around April 4, 2025, Defendant terminated the employment of approximately 200 employees at the Facilities ... that resulted in the total closure of the Facilities.' The bankruptcy first-day declaration says the same thing from the company's side: Declaration of Kasey Rosado, Chief Restructuring Officer, Case 2:25-bk-52140, Doc 16, filed 2025-05-16, paragraph 12, 'In February 2024, the Company achieved a significant milestone by opening the Advanced Manufacturing Enablement Center (AMEC) in New Albany, Ohio, a 350,000 square foot facility designed to provide flexible, multi-modality cGMP manufacturing suites for cell therapy, plasmid, mRNA, and gene editing products,' and paragraph 15, which distinguishes the owned West Jefferson real property from 'certain equipment left at their leased New Albany location.' I verified the county myself against the Licking County Auditor's own parcel service: parcel 093-107490-00.001, site address 9885 Innovation Campus Way, New Albany 43054, township JERSEY, tax district '093: JERSEY T-N ALB C-LK HTS LSD', school Licking Heights LSD, 33.054 acres, year built 2022, 351,846 square feet, class Industrial. The legal description carries 'TAX ABATE: 2024-2038 (100%) TIF 2023-2052' and the TIF field reads 'New Albany - District 4'. Market improvement value is $24,929,400 against a market total of $31,539,400. The ownership chain runs MBJ Holdings to Scannell Properties #538 LLC, to Mendel New Albany Property Owner LLC on 2024-10-03 for $35,850,000, to HMS New Albany OH LLC on 2026-02-06 for $88,250,000. A sweep of the whole Licking County parcel file for any owner containing 'AMPLIF' returns nothing. AmplifyBio's own site, at amplify-bio.com and not amplifybio.com, listed 'New Albany, Ohio - Manufacturing and Characterization Services (AMEC and ADOC Business Units) - 9885 Innovation Campus Way' and announced the grand opening on 2024-02-01, having said in November 2023 that 'Phase 1 of the 350,000-square-foot manufacturing facility will open in the first quarter of 2024,' so only part was ever fitted out. ADOC SSF, LLC is confirmed as the South San Francisco entity, the PACT Pharma intellectual property vehicle, and the declaration says the company closed its San Francisco location in late 2024. One wrinkle: by January 2025 the ADOC business unit had moved into the New Albany building, but the entity is still the SSF vehicle, so the Ohio picture is unchanged.

question: What did JobsOhio's $200,000 to Avelo Airlines buy, and what document says so?
answer: Purpose resolved; the dollar figure is not. A public primary record names JobsOhio money going to Avelo for Dayton to Orlando and names the program, the JobsOhio Commercial Air Service Restoration Program. No public document names the $200,000, or any dollar amount. And one of the project's working facts is wrong: JobsOhio did announce this route, with its own press release quoting its own chief executive, and has since deleted it. The archived release, page-dated Mon Nov 07 2022, carries J.P. Nauseef, JobsOhio president and CEO, verbatim: 'The JobsOhio Air Service Restoration Program was designed to bring more routes and seats to Ohio's commercial airports. Dayton International Airport serves an important market and draws from three Ohio metropolitan population areas. With strategic growth occurring in the region, we are hopeful the success of these routes will be the beginning of more air service at Dayton International.' It also quotes Governor Mike DeWine and Avelo chairman and CEO Andrew Levy, and gives the schedule: twice weekly Mondays and Fridays on Boeing Next-Generation 737s, inaugural flight Friday January 13. That URL now returns 404, redirecting to a blog path that also 404s, and JobsOhio's sitemap of 1,367 URLs contains no instance of 'avelo'. Dayton International Airport's own release of the same announcement survives on flydayton.com and adds Dayton Development Coalition president and CEO Jeff Hoagland: 'We're grateful to Avelo for seeing an opportunity here and to the City of Dayton and JobsOhio for supporting the new route. JobsOhio's Commercial Air Service Restoration Program works with communities to build new air travel routes to support economic development, and their partnership with Avelo represents a promising way for Dayton to grow our air service.' The removal is traceable frame by frame on JobsOhio's own program page. I pulled three snapshots myself: on 2023-02-02 the page contains the word Avelo zero times, before the route was live in JobsOhio's telling; on 2023-08-01 it contains it 13 times and reads 'JobsOhio has helped attract new carriers, including Breeze and Avelo, restore lost routes...'; on 2023-12-10 it contains it zero times and the same sentence reads 'JobsOhio has helped attract new carrier Breeze...', with the Dayton tab switched from Avelo and Orlando to United and Denver. The live page today still reads 'new carrier Breeze'. On the mechanism and the shape of the money, the program's board-approved guidelines are explicit. The Commercial Air Service Restoration Program was approved by the JobsOhio board on 2020-12-04 and amended on 2022-07-28 and 2026-06-16; only the 2026 version is posted, so the terms below are the current version, while the 2022-07-28 amendment is the one that would have governed the Avelo deal. It is funded at $10 million a fiscal year and works through 'short-term revenue guarantee incentives'. Domestic support is 'limited, short-term (up to 12 months) funding to support agreements with commercial air carriers'; JobsOhio will provide 'up to $1,000,000 for each domestic route'; and 'as an alternative to or in combination with the above support, JobsOhio may also provide up to $250,000 to be used for one-time costs associated with startup costs, equipment, and/or marketing and promotion'. The applicant is the airport, not the airline: the program is open to Ohio airports certified under FAA Part 139 'and any airline with a FAA Part 121 Commercial Operators Certificate', and a non-hub or small hub airport such as Dayton 'will provide a match that is up to 20% of the JobsOhio incentive commitment'. Leisure destinations like Orlando are eligible only 'on a case-by-case basis if there is a compelling economic and community impact'. The $200,000, split $160,000 in FY2023 and $40,000 in FY2024, sits inside the $250,000 one-time ceiling and well under the $1,000,000 route ceiling, and the twelve-month domestic cap matches a route that flew nine months. State that as a reading of the published ceilings against the Form 990 figures, because no document says it. The withholding is itself on the record: Dayton Daily News reported on 2023-08-24 that 'Avelo likely received financial incentives to operate its service out of Dayton, but local and state organizations declined to specify what kind of support the airline was given.'
